project.name: treetracker-wallet-admin-client
project.description: The admin panel for accessing wallets and executing all known API calls for the wallet API. Wallet owners use it to display and transfer tokens and transactions, create sub wallets, and configure their appearance.

nodes.name: transfers.js
nodes.summary: API module for the wallet API transfer endpoints: lists transfers with filter, pagination and sorting query strings, lists pending transfers, and sends accept, decline and cancel requests for one transfer.
nodes.languageNotes: The list calls go through the shared apiClient wrapper, but the accept, decline and cancel calls use the browser fetch API directly against `REACT_APP_WALLET_API_ROOT`, so they build their own headers and return the raw Response object.

nodes.name: getTransfers
nodes.summary: Builds a GET /transfers request from a TransferFilter where-object, pagination limits and optional sort_by/order values, then returns the response body; errors are logged and the call resolves to undefined.

nodes.name: getPendingTransfers
nodes.summary: Fetches only the transfers in the pending state through apiClient with the bearer token, used to count transfers that wait for an answer.

nodes.name: acceptTransfer
nodes.summary: Sends POST /transfers/{id}/accept with fetch to the `REACT_APP_WALLET_API_ROOT` base URL so the receiving wallet takes the offered tokens.

nodes.name: declineTransfer
nodes.summary: Sends POST /transfers/{id}/decline with fetch so the receiving wallet refuses a pending transfer; returns the raw fetch Response.

nodes.name: cancelTransfer
nodes.summary: Sends DELETE /transfers/{id} with fetch so the sending wallet withdraws a transfer that is still pending.

nodes.name: ClientRoutes.js
nodes.summary: Defines the React Router route table of the admin client: every page except /login sits behind a login guard and is wrapped in the trust relationship and transfers providers plus the shared Layout.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a React Router v6 layout route: a parent <Route element={<ProtectedRoute/>}> renders <Outlet/> for its nested routes, so the guard logic sits in one place.

nodes.name: ProtectedRoute
nodes.summary: Route guard component that renders the nested route Outlet when isLoggedIn is true and otherwise redirects with Navigate to /login (or a given redirectPath).

nodes.name: ClientRoutes
nodes.summary: Reads isLoggedIn from AuthContext and maps /, /my-transfers, /send-tokens, /list-wallets, /trust-relationship, /customize-wallet and a catch-all 404 route to their pages, with /login left public.

nodes.name: ClientRoutes.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest smoke test that renders ClientRoutes as a logged-in user and checks that the layout shows the Greenstand logo, seven links, seven buttons, and the Home and Send Tokens menu entries.

nodes.name: TestWrapper
nodes.summary: Test harness for the routes test that stacks the MUI theme, a BrowserRouter, an AuthContext value with isLoggedIn true and the TrustRelationshipsProvider around its children.

nodes.name: TransferFilter.js
nodes.summary: Model class for transfer list query options (state, wallet, before, after) that converts the chosen filter values into the where-object sent to the transfers API.
nodes.languageNotes: Declares public class fields and fills them with Object.assign(this, options) in the constructor, a compact way to build a typed-looking value object in plain JavaScript.

nodes.name: TransferFilter
nodes.summary: Value object holding the transfer filter options; getWhereObj lowercases the state and formats before/after dates as YYYY-MM-DD so the API gets only the fields that are set.

nodes.name: CustomizeWallet.js
nodes.summary: Customize Wallet page where a wallet owner edits the display name, the rich-text about text, the logo and the hero image; each field saves on its own through updateWallet and shows a timed success or error message.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses FileReader plus an Image object inside a Promise to read the real pixel width and height of a chosen file before it is uploaded, which lets the page check the aspect ratio in the browser.

nodes.name: CustomizeWallet
nodes.summary: Page component that loads the current wallet by the id kept in localStorage, keeps form state and previews for the four editable fields, and renders the inputs with a ReactQuill editor and hidden file inputs.

nodes.name: validateImageFile
nodes.summary: Throws a user-readable error when no file is chosen, when the file exceeds the size limit (1 MB), or when its type is not PNG or JPEG.

nodes.name: handleImageChange
nodes.summary: Validates a chosen logo or hero file, reads it as a data URL, and checks its dimensions (square for the logo, width at least twice the height for the hero) before it sets the preview.

nodes.name: handleImageUpload
nodes.summary: Runs handleImageChange and, if the image passes, sends the file as logoImage or coverImage through updateWallet; it maps a "File too large" server error to a friendlier message.

nodes.name: TransfersContext.js
nodes.summary: React context that owns the transfers list state (pagination, filter, sorting, rows, total, loading, messages) and the pending-transfer count of the logged-in and managed wallets, refetching when any of them change.
nodes.languageNotes: Pairs a provider with a custom hook that throws when used outside the provider, which turns a silent undefined context into a clear error.

nodes.name: TransfersProvider
nodes.summary: Context provider that defines the status list and table column config, runs loadData whenever pagination, filter, sorting or refetch change, and loads the pending count on refetch.

nodes.name: useTransfersContext
nodes.summary: Custom hook that returns the transfers context value and throws an error when a component calls it outside TransfersProvider.

nodes.name: prepareRows
nodes.summary: Maps raw API transfer records into table rows, adding display keys (transfer_id, sender_wallet, receiver_wallet, token_amount, status) while it keeps the original API field names.

nodes.name: loadData
nodes.summary: Fetches the current page of transfers with getTransfers using the context pagination, filter and sorting, stores the prepared rows and total, and resets the refetch flag.

nodes.name: loadPendingTransfersData
nodes.summary: Loads up to 1000 child (managed) wallets with getWallets, then counts pending transfers whose destination is the logged-in wallet or a managed wallet; Layout reads this count.

nodes.name: auth-context.js
nodes.summary: Creates the AuthContext React context whose default value describes the login state shape: isLoggedIn, token, wallet, and login/logout functions.

nodes.name: AuthContext
nodes.summary: React context object (not a function) that pages and providers read with useContext to get the access token and logout; AuthProvider supplies its live value.

nodes.name: formatting.js
nodes.summary: Shared formatting helpers: locale number formatting with thousands separators, dayjs date-to-text formatting, and conversion of a filter object into a URL query string.
nodes.languageNotes: formatWithCommas reads `process.env.USER_LOCALE`; that name lacks the `REACT_APP_` prefix, so react-scripts does not embed it in the browser bundle and Intl.NumberFormat falls back to the browser default locale.

nodes.name: formatWithCommas
nodes.summary: One-line helper that formats a number with Intl.NumberFormat for the `USER_LOCALE` locale, used for token amounts in tables.

nodes.name: getDateText
nodes.summary: Formats any dayjs-parsable date value (dayjs object or ISO string) into text with the given pattern, such as MM/DD/YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD.

nodes.name: makeQueryString
nodes.summary: Joins the keys of a filter object into a key=value&key=value query string and skips keys whose value is null or an empty string.

nodes.name: trust_relationships.js
nodes.summary: Client for the wallet API trust relationship endpoints: it lists, filters, requests, accepts, declines, and deletes relationships, and pages through trusted wallets. List and request calls use the shared apiClient, while accept, decline, and delete use native fetch against REACT_APP_WALLET_API_ROOT.
nodes.languageNotes: Mixes two HTTP styles: the chained apiClient.setAuthHeader(token).get/post wrapper and native fetch with hand-built headers. Several functions log and swallow errors, so callers receive undefined instead of an exception.

nodes.name: getTrustRelationships
nodes.summary: Fetches one page of trust relationships for the wallet saved in localStorage, merging pagination, the filter object's getWhereObj() output, and sort_by/order into a query string with makeQueryString. It logs failures and returns undefined instead of throwing.

nodes.name: getPendingTrustRelationships
nodes.summary: Requests every trust relationship in the `requested` state for the current localStorage wallet; the context store uses the result to count requests that wait for the user's answer.

nodes.name: requestTrustRelationship
nodes.summary: POSTs a new trust request to /trust_relationships, mapping the form fields requestType, requestingWallet, and targetWallet to the API fields trust_request_type, requester_wallet, and requestee_wallet. It rethrows failures with the server message appended so the dialog can show it.

nodes.name: acceptTrustRelationship
nodes.summary: Accepts a pending trust relationship with a native fetch POST to /trust_relationships/{id}/accept and returns the raw Response without checking its status code.

nodes.name: declineTrustRelationship
nodes.summary: Declines a pending trust relationship with a POST to /trust_relationships/{id}/decline; like the accept call, it returns the unchecked fetch Response and only logs network errors.

nodes.name: deleteTrustRelationship
nodes.summary: Sends DELETE /trust_relationships/{id}, parses the JSON body when there is one, and throws an Error with the server message or the HTTP status on a non-OK reply, so the side panel can display the reason.

nodes.name: getTrustedWallets
nodes.summary: Pages through all trusted relationships of a given sender wallet in chunks of 500, keeps only `send` relationships where that wallet is the actor, and returns de-duplicated target wallets shaped for wallet pickers (id, name, tokensInWallet 0).

nodes.name: getAllTrustedWallets
nodes.summary: Collects every wallet that a trusted relationship links to the current localStorage wallet, taking target, actor, and originator candidates, skipping the wallet itself, de-duplicating by name, and sorting the list alphabetically.

nodes.name: Message.js

nodes.name: MessageType
nodes.summary: Constant map of the four MUI Alert severities (error, warning, info, success) that pages pass as the messageType prop to pick a banner color and icon.

nodes.name: Message
nodes.summary: Renders an inline-block MUI Alert with the given text and close callback, and falls back to the error severity when the caller supplies no messageType.

nodes.name: Message.test.js

nodes.name: TrustRelationshipsFilter
nodes.summary: Filter value object built with Object.assign from an options bag; getWhereObj() emits only the fields that are set, lowercases text values, and formats before/after as YYYY-MM-DD with getDateText. Components create a new instance on every filter change.

nodes.summary: MUI Drawer styled from its open prop, which it keeps off the DOM; it applies openedMixin or closedMixin to both the root and the .MuiDrawer-paper element.

nodes.name: BoldTypography
nodes.summary: Bold 0.9rem Typography for the field labels (Source Wallet, Target Wallet, Initiated By, Request Type) in the detail drawer.

nodes.name: NormalTypography
nodes.summary: Regular-weight, capitalized 0.9rem Typography that holds the field values next to the bold labels in the detail drawer.

nodes.name: TallTypography
nodes.summary: Typography with a fixed 40px height and top-left flex alignment; the file exports it, but no file in the project imports it.

nodes.name: DeclineButton
nodes.summary: Borderless text button in orange #FF7A00 that declines a pending trust request from the detail drawer.

nodes.name: DeleteButton
nodes.summary: Borderless white-text button that sits on a red rounded box in the drawer and deletes a trusted or outgoing relationship.

nodes.name: AcceptButton
nodes.summary: Contained button with a 20px corner radius and medium-weight text that accepts a pending trust request in the drawer.

nodes.name: TrustRelationshipTable.js
nodes.summary: Main trust relationships table: a header with title, create button, wallet search, and filter menu; sortable column titles; a body that tints requests that wait for the user's answer and opens a detail drawer on row click; and server-side pagination through the trust relationships context.
nodes.languageNotes: Splits one screen into several local arrow-function components in one module, with only the container exported. A stray `('react');` expression statement on line 26 has no effect.

nodes.name: FilterDialog
nodes.summary: Anchored MUI Menu (kept mounted) that groups the state, request type, and type select filters with a Clear Filters reset button; the date range filter and an Apply button are commented out.

nodes.name: TrustRelationshipTableHeader
nodes.summary: Header row that shows the table title, the CreateTrustRelationship button, a search field that writes a new TrustRelationshipsFilter with the search text on each keystroke, and a Filters button that toggles FilterDialog.

nodes.name: OverflownCell
nodes.summary: Table cell that compares its scrollWidth with its clientWidth after mount and enables a hover tooltip with the full value only when the text overflows.

nodes.name: TrustRelationshipTableBody
nodes.summary: Renders a loader, an empty-state row, or the data rows. Requested rows that target the current wallet or a managed wallet get a light green tint, and a click selects the row and opens TrustRelationshipSidePanel. It also filters rows on the context searchString, which nothing in the project sets, so that filter passes every row.

nodes.name: TrustRelationshipTable
nodes.summary: Default-exported table container that keeps local page, rows-per-page, sort column, and order state, sends pagination and sorting changes to the context, and renders the header, sortable column titles with arrow icons, the body, and TablePagination with 10 or 50 rows.

nodes.name: handleRowsPerPageChange
nodes.summary: Pagination handler that parses the new rows-per-page value, resets the page to 0, and sends limit and offset 0 to the context, so the list reloads from the first row.

nodes.name: getColumnNames
nodes.summary: Maps a column name to its API sort key; every switch branch returns the input unchanged, so it is an identity function at present.

nodes.name: handleSort
nodes.summary: Column click handler that changes to descending order when the same column is already sorted ascending (it also matches the wallet_name/name and created_date/created_at aliases) and sends the new sort_by and order to the context.

nodes.name: TrustRelationshipsFilters.js
nodes.summary: Filter controls for the trust relationships table: select menus for state, request type, and type, a Clear Filters button, and a date range popover with two date pickers. Each control writes a new TrustRelationshipsFilter instance through setFilter.

nodes.name: StateSelectFilter
nodes.summary: Select control labelled State with an "All" option plus the statesList entries; a change creates a new TrustRelationshipsFilter with the chosen state.

nodes.name: RequestTypeSelectFilter
nodes.summary: Request Type select that lists the requestTypeList options (manage, send, deduct, receive, release, yield) and stores the choice as request_type on a new filter object.

nodes.name: TypeSelectFilter
nodes.summary: Type select over typeList (manage, send, deduct) that sets the filter type field; it carries the type-select-filter test id that the page test looks for.

nodes.name: ResetButton
nodes.summary: Orange "Clear Filters" text button that restores the defaultFilter from the context and then closes the filter menu.

nodes.name: DateRangeFilter
nodes.summary: Created Date filter that opens a popover with start and end DatePickers (no future dates, start not after end) and applies after/before only on OK. Its button label is commented out, and the table does not render this filter.

nodes.name: handleOK
nodes.summary: Applies the chosen start and end dates as after and before on a new TrustRelationshipsFilter, then closes the date popover.

nodes.name: TrustRelationshipsFilters.styled.js
nodes.summary: Emotion styled MUI parts for the trust relationship filter controls: bold captions, borderless select boxes with a hover outline, menu items, the drop-down arrow, and the date range button and icon. It also exports a FilterResetButton that no file imports.

nodes.name: FilterLabelText
nodes.summary: Bold 16px Typography with a 24px line height used as the caption above each filter control (State, Request Type, Type, Created Date).

nodes.name: SelectFilter
nodes.summary: MUI Select, 40px high, with a light grey border, a hidden notched outline, a transparent focus background, and a black hover border; it is the shared shell of the three select filters.

nodes.name: SelectMenuItem
nodes.summary: MenuItem with 16px text used for the "All" entry and for each option inside the filter select menus.

nodes.name: ArrowDropDownIcon
nodes.summary: 24px ArrowDropDown icon that the filter selects use as IconComponent and the date range button uses as its end icon.

nodes.name: DateFilterTitle
nodes.summary: Grid item laid out as a space-between flex row that holds the "Enter dates" heading and the calendar icon in the date popover.

nodes.name: DateRangeButton
nodes.summary: Outlined-look 40px button with grey, non-uppercase text and start/end icons that opens the date range popover.

nodes.name: DateRangeFilterIcon
nodes.summary: Green #86c232 DateRangeIcon from MUI X date pickers, used as the start icon of the date range button.

nodes.name: FilterResetButton
nodes.summary: White-text 2.5rem Button style exported for a reset action; the trust relationship filters use a plain button instead, so nothing imports this export.

nodes.name: TrustRelationshipsFilters.test.js
nodes.summary: Test file for the filter controls that builds a default TrustRelationshipsFilter and a mock setter. Its only test, which opens the State select and picks "Requested", is skipped, so the file runs no assertions at present.

nodes.name: trustRelationshipSidePanel.js
nodes.summary: Right-side detail drawer for one trust relationship row: it shows source, target, initiator, and request type with truncating tooltips, and offers Accept and Decline when a request targets the user's wallet or a managed wallet, else Delete. After an action it closes and sets refetch so the context reloads.

nodes.name: TrustRelationshipSidePanel
nodes.summary: Drawer component that reads managed wallets, setRefetch, and setMessage from the context and the token from AuthContext. Accept and Decline start their API calls without awaiting them before the refetch, while Delete waits for its result.

nodes.name: handleDelete
nodes.summary: Awaits deleteTrustRelationship for the row id, then closes the drawer and requests a refetch; on failure it puts the server error text into the context message banner.

nodes.name: TrustRelationshipsContext.js
nodes.summary: React context store for the trust relationships feature: it holds pagination, sorting, filter, column definitions, option lists, rows, total count, loading and error state, and the count of pending requests that Layout reads. It reloads data when pagination, filter, sorting, or refetch change.
nodes.languageNotes: Both data effects depend on refetch, and loadData resets refetch to false in finally, so one action that sets refetch to true causes a second round of both loads when the flag flips back.

nodes.name: TrustRelationshipsProvider
nodes.summary: Context provider that defines the defaults (10 rows, empty filter, sort by state descending), the column definitions with MM/DD/YYYY date renderers, and the state, request type, and type option lists, and exposes all state, setters, and loadData to the feature components.

nodes.name: prepareRows
nodes.summary: Maps raw API trust relationship records to table rows that keep only id, type, state, request_type, the two timestamps, and the originating, actor, and target wallet names.

nodes.name: loadData
nodes.summary: Fetches the current page with getTrustRelationships from pagination, filter, and sorting, stores the prepared rows and the total, sets an error message on failure, and always clears the loading and refetch flags.

nodes.name: loadPendingRelationshipsData
nodes.summary: Loads up to 1000 child-scope managed wallets with getWallets, then counts requested relationships whose target is the current wallet or one of those managed wallets, and stores that number as count.

nodes.name: useTrustRelationshipsContext
nodes.summary: Custom hook that returns the trust relationships context and throws a clear error when a component calls it outside TrustRelationshipsProvider.

nodes.name: TabPanel.js
nodes.summary: Generic MUI tab panel wrapper that renders its children in a padded Box only when its index matches the active tab value, with the tabpanel role and ARIA ids. The Send Tokens page uses it for its three wallet tabs.

nodes.name: TabPanel
nodes.summary: Functional component that reads value, index, and children from props, hides its wrapping div when the tab is not active, and passes all other props (for example style) through to that div.

nodes.name: PageHeader.js
nodes.summary: Shared layout component that shows a page title in a styled MUI CardHeader. The Send Tokens and Customize Wallet pages use it as their page heading.

nodes.name: PageHeader
nodes.summary: Renders StyledCardHeader with the title prop as its text, which gives each page the same header with a fixed top margin and vertical padding.

nodes.name: PageHeaderStyled.js
nodes.summary: Emotion styling module for the page header that wraps MUI CardHeader with a 6.6vh top margin and 2rem top and bottom padding.

nodes.name: StyledCardHeader
nodes.summary: Emotion styled() version of MUI CardHeader that adds the viewport-relative top margin and the vertical padding that PageHeader relies on.

nodes.name: SendTokens.js
nodes.summary: Route-level Send Tokens page that holds the selected sender wallet, its token balance, and its pending outgoing amount, and shows three tabs (Managed Wallets, Trusted Wallets, All Wallets) with the matching transfer form and a TokenInfoBlock. It loads trusted wallet lists from the trust relationships API, refreshes balances from the wallets API, and posts transfers through apiClient or the helper handlers.
nodes.languageNotes: A React function component with many useState hooks builds a callbacks object of state setters and passes it to plain async helper functions, so the helpers can update page state without being hooks.

nodes.name: SendTokens
nodes.summary: Main page component that manages the active tab, error and success messages, loading state, and the sender wallet, resets the sender on each tab change, and loads trusted wallets for tab 1 or all trusted wallets for tab 2 in an effect. It renders Message alerts, a Loader overlay, and one TabPanel per tab with SendTokensForm or SendToUntrustedWalletsForm next to TokenInfoBlock.

nodes.name: loadTrustedWallets
nodes.summary: Fetches the wallets that have a send trust relationship with the given sender wallet through getTrustedWallets, removes entries with duplicate ids, and stores the list for the Trusted Wallets tab.

nodes.name: loadAllTrustedWallets
nodes.summary: Loads the complete list from getAllTrustedWallets when the All Wallets tab opens, so that the free-text receiver field can suggest wallet names, and sets an error message if the request fails.

nodes.name: refreshWalletData
nodes.summary: Re-reads the sender wallet with getWalletById and its pending outgoing total, then updates the tokens-in-wallet and pending-transfer state so that the available balance stays correct after a selection or a transfer.

nodes.name: handleWalletSelection
nodes.summary: Callback for the sender wallet picker: it clears the sender name, id, tokens, and pending amount when the selection is removed, and otherwise stores the wallet name and id and calls refreshWalletData.

nodes.name: handleSendTokenForm
nodes.summary: Page-local transfer submit that posts a bundle of tokensAmount from sender to receiver to /transfers with claim false, refreshes the sender wallet after success, and keeps the API text only for the same-wallet error. The Managed and Trusted tabs use this version, not the helper with the same name.

nodes.name: SelectWallet.js
nodes.summary: Reusable MUI Autocomplete for picking a wallet by name. It searches the wallets API with an optional scope, pages results 10 at a time behind a Load more option, can add the logged-in wallet from localStorage, and filters a given list on the client when walletType is trusted.
nodes.languageNotes: Exported through React.memo. A LOAD_MORE sentinel string inside the options array makes renderOption draw a button row in the dropdown.

nodes.name: SelectWallet
nodes.summary: Memoized wallet picker component with three effects: one fetches or filters wallets when the search text, type, scope, or trusted list changes, one selects a newly created wallet by name, and one appends the next page after Load more. On change it gives onChangeWallet the full wallet object instead of only the name.

nodes.name: SendToUntrustedWallets.js
nodes.summary: Transfer form for the All Wallets tab. The sender comes from SelectWallet with child scope, the receiver is a free-text Autocomplete seeded with all trusted wallet names, and the token amount is checked against the available balance before a ConfirmDialog asks for confirmation.

nodes.name: SendToUntrustedWalletsForm
nodes.summary: Memoized form component that keeps sender, receiver address, and amount state, keeps Submit disabled until all fields are valid, and opens ConfirmDialog on submit. After the user confirms, it calls onSubmit with senderWallet, receiverWallet, and tokensAmount.

nodes.name: validateTokenAmount
nodes.summary: Amount check of the untrusted-wallet form: it passes while no sender is selected, and otherwise flags a value of zero or less, or a value larger than availableTokens, with a helper message.

nodes.name: handleChangeSenderWallet
nodes.summary: useCallback handler of the untrusted-wallet form that stores the chosen sender name, reports the wallet object to the page through onSenderWalletSelected, and re-validates the amount; a cleared selection also clears the amount error.

nodes.name: handleSubmit
nodes.summary: Reads the amount from the input ref, sends the sender, the typed receiver address, and the amount to onSubmit, and resets the amount field of the untrusted-wallet form to 1.

nodes.name: SendTokensForm.js
nodes.summary: Transfer form for the Managed Wallets and Trusted Wallets tabs: two SelectWallet pickers for sender and receiver, an inline Create Managed Wallet field with name validation for the managed type, a token amount input limited by availableTokens, and a ConfirmDialog step before submit.

nodes.name: SendTokensForm
nodes.summary: Memoized form component that holds sender and receiver names, the create-wallet toggle and its errors, and amount errors, and gives the receiver picker the walletType, trustedWallets, and a child scope for managed wallets. It calls onCreateWallet for a new managed wallet and onSubmit after the user confirms in ConfirmDialog.

nodes.name: handleChangeSenderWallet
nodes.summary: Sender change handler of the managed and trusted form that first clears the chosen receiver, then stores or clears the sender name, notifies the page, and re-checks the amount input.

nodes.name: validateCreateWallet
nodes.summary: Checks a new managed wallet name: it must not be empty and may contain only letters, digits, hyphen, dot, and @. On failure it sets the error flag and helper text of the name field.

nodes.name: validateTokenAmount
nodes.summary: Validates the managed or trusted transfer amount against the sender balance: no error without a sender, an error for values of zero or less, and a locale-formatted Available message when the value exceeds availableTokens.

nodes.name: handleSubmit
nodes.summary: Collects senderWallet, receiverWallet, and the ref-held token amount, logs the amount, calls the onSubmit prop from the page, and puts the amount input back to 1 after the confirmed transfer.

nodes.name: SendTokensFormStyled.js
nodes.summary: Emotion styled wrappers shared by both Send Tokens forms: a growing Box with 2rem margin and a 60rem maximum width, and a Button that is only as wide as its label.

nodes.name: StyledBox
nodes.summary: MUI Box styled with flexGrow 1, a 2rem margin, and a 60rem max width; it is the outer container of SendTokensForm and SendToUntrustedWalletsForm.

nodes.name: StyledButton
nodes.summary: MUI Button styled through an Emotion template literal with width fit-content, used as the Submit button of both transfer forms.

nodes.name: ConfirmDialog.js
nodes.summary: Transfer confirmation dialog that asks "Are you sure to make this transfer?" and shows stacked token icons, the sender and receiver wallets with an arrow between them, the amount, and No and Yes buttons.

nodes.name: TokenIConPositioned
nodes.summary: Small helper component that places one TokenICon in an absolutely positioned div at the given top, left, and zIndex; the dialog stacks three of them to draw a pile of tokens.

nodes.name: WalletInfo
nodes.summary: Helper component that shows a grey round avatar icon next to a wallet name in a horizontal Stack, used for both the sender side and the receiver side of the dialog.

nodes.name: ConfirmDialog
nodes.summary: Default-exported MUI Dialog component that takes open, onConfirm, onClose, senderWallet, receiverWallet, and a tokensAmount ref, and reads the amount from tokensAmount.current.value when it renders.

nodes.name: SvgIcon.js
nodes.summary: Inline SVG icon components for the transfer confirmation dialog: a person avatar in a grey circle, a long right-pointing arrow, and a green token coin with a seedling mark. Most of its lines are SVG path and shape markup.

nodes.name: AvatarSvgIcon
nodes.summary: Renders a 25px MUI SvgIcon person silhouette centered in a 70 by 50 grey rounded Box, which serves as the wallet avatar in the dialog.

nodes.name: ArrowSvgIcon
nodes.summary: Raw 279 by 24 SVG of a horizontal line with a chevron head that points from the sender wallet to the receiver wallet.

nodes.name: TokenICon
nodes.summary: Raw 91 by 91 SVG of two overlapping outlined circles, five tick marks, and a leaf and seed shape in green (#86C232), drawn as the token coin.

nodes.name: SendTokensStyled.js
nodes.summary: Emotion styled layout pieces for the Send Tokens page: a full-width grid root, a flex content container with no max width from 1200px, a responsive card grid, and a centered absolute loader overlay.

nodes.name: StyledGrid
nodes.summary: MUI Grid with width 100%, used as the outermost wrapper element of the Send Tokens page.

nodes.name: ContentContainer
nodes.summary: MUI Container set to flex with items at the start and space between, zero margin, and maxWidth unset from 1200px wide, so that the tab Paper can fill the page.

nodes.name: ContentGrid
nodes.summary: CSS grid of 20rem cells with a 2rem gap and media queries at 768px and 480px; it is exported, but SendTokens does not import it.

nodes.name: LoaderContainer
nodes.summary: Plain div styled to sit at the center of its parent with absolute position, a translate transform, and zIndex 9999, so that the Loader shows above the forms.

nodes.name: TokenInfoBlock.js
nodes.summary: Balance panel that appears next to a transfer form after a sender is chosen. It lists tokens in wallet, tokens pending transfer, and tokens available, each as a locale-formatted number with a green label.

nodes.name: TokenInfoBlock
nodes.summary: Component that takes inWallet, pendingTransfer, and available props, uses inWallet minus pendingTransfer when available is 0, and lays out the three rows with a token icon and divider lines in an MUI Grid.

nodes.name: TokenInfoBlock.test.js
nodes.summary: Jest test file for TokenInfoBlock and SendTokens that mocks apiClient.get and puts a test wallet in localStorage, but all three test bodies have their render and expect calls commented out with TODO notes, so they assert nothing.

nodes.name: TokenInfoBlockStyled.js
nodes.summary: MUI system styled Typography variants for TokenInfoBlock: a 16px bold centered green label style and a 24px bold centered green amount style.

nodes.name: SubText
nodes.summary: Typography styled at 16px bold in rgb(97,137,47) with center alignment and 10px padding, used for row labels such as Tokens In Wallet.

nodes.name: AmountText
nodes.summary: Typography styled at 24px bold in the same green with vertical padding only, used for the numeric amount in each TokenInfoBlock row.

nodes.name: sendTokenHandlers.js
nodes.summary: Async transfer helpers for the Send Tokens page. Each takes form data, the auth context, and a callbacks object of state setters, posts to /transfers, refreshes or decrements the sender balance, and turns API errors into user messages.

nodes.name: handleSendTokenForm
nodes.summary: Helper that posts a bundle transfer with claim false, calls refreshWalletData when a senderWalletId is given or else subtracts the amount from the sender tokens, and keeps the same-wallet API message. No file imports it at present, because SendTokens has its own copy.

nodes.name: handleSendToUntrustedWallets
nodes.summary: Transfer helper for the All Wallets tab that posts the same /transfers payload, adds a note that the receiver is not trusted to the success text, and maps same-wallet, invalid wallet address, and HTTP 403 errors to specific messages.

nodes.name: walletHandlers.js
nodes.summary: Single async helper module that creates a managed wallet through apiClient for the Send Tokens page and reports the outcome through state-setter callbacks.

nodes.name: handleCreateWallet
nodes.summary: Posts the new wallet name to /wallets with the auth token, sets a success message and createdWalletName on success, and shows "Wallet with this name already exists." when the API answers 403 with an already exists message.

nodes.name: apiClient.js
nodes.summary: Shared axios instance for the wallet API. Its base URL comes from REACT_APP_WALLET_API_ROOT, a TREETRACKER-API-KEY header is read from react-secure-storage, chainable helpers set the auth and content-type headers, and a response interceptor handles 401 responses with a navigation to /login.
nodes.languageNotes: Custom methods are attached directly to the axios instance and return it, which allows chained calls such as apiClient.setAuthHeader(token).post(...).

nodes.name: apiClient
nodes.summary: Default-exported axios instance created with axios.create and then extended with header helper methods and a response interceptor; the API modules and the Send Tokens helpers import it for wallet API requests.

nodes.name: setAPIKeyHeader
nodes.summary: Sets the TREETRACKER-API-KEY default header from the given key, or from the api-key entry of secure storage when no key is given, and returns the instance; the Login page calls it.

nodes.name: setAuthToken
nodes.summary: Adds an Authorization Bearer header to the common axios defaults when a token is given, and deletes that header when the token is empty.

nodes.name: setAuthHeader
nodes.summary: Chainable wrapper that calls setAuthToken with the token and returns apiClient, so that callers can write apiClient.setAuthHeader(token).post(...).

nodes.name: addContentType
nodes.summary: Sets the default Content-Type header when a value is given and returns the instance; the wallets API uses it with multipart/form-data for uploads.

nodes.name: App.js
nodes.summary: Root React component that stacks the app-wide providers: the MUI theme, a Day.js date-picker localization adapter, BrowserRouter, and AuthProvider, around ClientRoutes and the main Layout.

nodes.name: App
nodes.summary: Returns the provider tree for the whole admin panel so every page gets theming, date localization, routing, and auth context before ClientRoutes decides what to render inside Layout.

nodes.name: App.test.js
nodes.summary: Smoke test that renders the full App with react-secure-storage mocked and checks that an unauthenticated visitor lands on the login screen with its logo, Wallet Admin Panel heading, credential fields, and LOG IN button.

nodes.name: wallets.js
nodes.summary: Wallet API client module that wraps the shared apiClient to list, fetch, create, and update wallets and to read a wallet's pending transfers, converting API payloads into the camelCase shape the UI uses.
nodes.languageNotes: Mixes promise chains (.then/.catch inside await) with a plain try/catch; getWallets destructures nested default parameter objects so callers can pass only pagination, sorting, or scope.

nodes.name: mapWallet
nodes.summary: Normalizes one raw wallet record into the UI shape (logoURL, coverURL, tokensInWallet, displayName, and so on), taking the name field key as a parameter because list and detail endpoints return the wallet name under different properties.

nodes.name: getWallets
nodes.summary: Requests GET /wallets with an optional name filter, offset and limit pagination, sort_by and order, and a scope value, then returns the total count plus wallets mapped through mapWallet; defaults to the first 10 wallets, newest first.

nodes.name: getWalletById
nodes.summary: Fetches a single wallet from GET /wallets/:id and maps it with the 'wallet' property as the wallet name, rethrowing a generic fetch error on failure.

nodes.name: createWallet
nodes.summary: Posts a new managed wallet name to POST /wallets and returns the created record, surfacing the server's error message so the create dialog can show it to the user.

nodes.name: updateWallet
nodes.summary: Sends a multipart PATCH to /wallets/:id with about text, display name, and new cover and logo images, used to save wallet customization changes.

nodes.name: getPendingTransfers
nodes.summary: Reads the pending transfers of one wallet from GET /wallets/:walletId/pending-transfers with async/await and try/catch, and returns the raw response body.

nodes.name: theme.js
nodes.summary: Material UI theme module for the whole admin panel, defining the Lato typography, the Greenstand green palette with custom shades and a stats color set, and style overrides for buttons, lists, selects, toggle buttons, tables, MUI-Datatables header cells, and alerts. It also exports the colorPrimary constant.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the MUI v5 components.<Name>.styleOverrides and defaultProps API; the trailing top-level props key follows the older MUI v4 convention and has no effect in v5.

nodes.name: theme
nodes.summary: Default-exported createTheme result that App.js and the test wrappers pass to ThemeProvider: 4px spacing unit, 11px base font, primary rgba(118, 187, 35), outlined buttons by default, and green hover and selected states for list items, table rows, and selects.

nodes.name: index.js
nodes.summary: Browser entry point that creates a React 18 root on the #root element, renders App, loads the global index.css, and calls reportWebVitals without a callback so no metrics are sent.

nodes.name: Login.test.js
nodes.summary: Render test for the Login page that checks the Greenstand logo, the single Wallet Admin Panel heading, the Wallet, API Key, and password fields, and the LOG IN and password visibility buttons.

nodes.name: TestWrapper
nodes.summary: Test harness for the login render test that wraps children in the app theme, a BrowserRouter, and the real AuthProvider so Login can use navigation and auth context.

nodes.name: CreateManagedWallet.js
nodes.summary: Managed wallet creation feature for the My Wallets page: a Create Managed Wallet button opens an MUI dialog that validates the name, calls the createWallet API with the session token, shows a success state, and asks the parent to reload its list.

nodes.name: CreateManagedWallet
nodes.summary: Default-exported component that renders the styled Create Managed Wallet button and owns the open or closed state of the creation dialog, forwarding the parent's loadData callback to it.

nodes.name: CreateNewWalletDialog
nodes.summary: Dialog component with a Wallet Name text field, Cancel and Create actions, and a close icon; it keeps the input, error message, and success flag in state and swaps the form for a success icon and message after creation.

nodes.name: validateCreateWallet
nodes.summary: Client-side check for a new wallet name: requires a value, at least 3 characters, and only letters, digits, hyphen, dot, and at sign, and sets the matching helper text when a rule fails.

nodes.name: handleCreateWallet
nodes.summary: Create button handler that stops on failed validation, otherwise calls createWallet with the AuthContext token, sets the success flag, clears the input, and calls loadData; API errors become the field's helper text.

nodes.name: CreateManagedWallet.test.js
nodes.summary: Interaction tests for the managed wallet dialog with the wallets API mocked: the button opens the dialog with its controls, validation messages appear for empty, too short, and invalid names, close and Cancel dismiss it, and a valid name shows the success message.

nodes.name: TestWrapper
nodes.summary: Provider stack for the managed wallet dialog tests: app theme, BrowserRouter, the real AuthProvider, and WalletsProvider around the rendered children.

nodes.name: MyWallets.js
nodes.summary: My Wallets page that lists the logged-in wallet's wallets in the shared Table, with a scope selector for all, child, or managed wallets, server-side pagination and sorting from WalletsContext, a Create Managed Wallet button, and an error Message.

nodes.name: MyWallets
nodes.summary: Page component that pulls pagination, sorting, loading state, column definitions, and the row mapper from useWalletsContext, keeps the rows, total count, error text, and scope (default child) in local state, and reloads whenever pagination, sorting, or scope changes.

nodes.name: loadData
nodes.summary: Async loader inside MyWallets that calls getWallets with the session token, current pagination, sorting, and selected scope, converts the result with prepareRows, and stores rows and total, showing an error message on failure.

nodes.name: MyWallets.style.js
nodes.summary: Emotion styled-component module that defines the flex column layout container for the My Wallets page.

nodes.name: Container
nodes.summary: Styled div used as the My Wallets page root: flex column, 5rem top margin, 1rem side margins, and full width.

nodes.name: MyWallets.test.js
nodes.summary: Page test for My Wallets that mocks getWallets with a 12-wallet fixture, seeds a logged-in wallet in localStorage around each test, and checks that the table, its pagination, and 13 rows (12 data rows plus the header) render.

nodes.name: TestWrapper
nodes.summary: Wrapper used by the My Wallets page test that nests the rendered page inside ThemeProvider, BrowserRouter, AuthProvider, and WalletsProvider so the page can read the token and table state.

nodes.name: TrustRelationshipTable.test.js
nodes.summary: Test file for TrustRelationshipTable with four mocked trust relationship rows (send and manage requests, requested and trusted states); its only test is skipped with a todo, so the table, filter, and pagination checks do not currently run.

nodes.name: TestWrapper
nodes.summary: Wrapper for the trust relationship table test that adds TrustRelationshipsProvider inside the theme, router, and AuthProvider layers, giving the table its filter and pagination context.

nodes.name: trustRelationshipSidePanel.test.js
nodes.summary: Render test for the trust relationship side panel that mocks the trust relationship API calls and getWallets, opens the panel for a requested send relationship, and checks the Source Wallet, Target Wallet, Initiated By, and Request Type labels and the wallet name text.

nodes.name: TestWrapper

nodes.name: build-release.yaml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow "Build and Release" that runs on every branch push: it lints, builds and tests the client, runs semantic-release, and syncs the `npm run build:dev` bundle (`build-dev`, uploaded as the `client-bundle` artifact) to an S3 bucket, then invalidates the CloudFront cache. A prepare job reads `.releaserc.json`, skips the build for branches outside its list, and maps channel `main` to the `DEV_CDN_S3_BUCKET` and `DEV_CDN_DISTRIBUTION_ID` secrets and channel `beta` (branches `v1` and `v2`) to the `DEV_STAGING_CDN_S3_BUCKET` and `DEV_STAGING_CDN_DISTRIBUTION_ID` secrets.
nodes.languageNotes: The prepare job runs an inline Node heredoc that prints `KEY=value` lines into `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, and the deploy job then looks up secrets by a computed name with `secrets[needs.prepare.outputs.S3_BUCKET_SECRET_NAME]`. The `release` and `deploy` job conditions embed `${{ github.env.repository }}` inside an `if:` expression; the `github` context has no `env` property, so that repository check probably does not work as written.

nodes.name: deploy.yaml
nodes.summary: Manually dispatched GitHub Actions workflow "Deploy" that checks out a release tag (input `version`), builds it for the input `env` value `dev`, `test` or `prod`, syncs the `frontend-bundle` artifact to the matching S3 bucket and invalidates CloudFront. The prepare job checks out branch `v2` to read `.releaserc.json`, derives the channel (`main` for a plain `vX.Y.Z`, else the prerelease channel such as `beta`) and resolves secret names keyed by `<channel>-<env>`; the frontend job runs `npm run build` for `prod`, `npm run build:test` for `test` and `npm run build:dev` for `dev`.
nodes.languageNotes: For `env` = `dev`, the `build:dev` script renames `build` to `build-dev`, but the upload step reads `build`, so the `frontend-bundle` artifact is probably empty on that path. The AWS credential secrets are chosen with the `case()` expression function (`AWS_KEY_ID_PROD` and `AWS_SECRET_PROD` for `prod`, `AWS_KEY_ID_DEV` and `AWS_SECRET_DEV` otherwise). Unlike build-release.yaml, the CDN distribution secret name has no missing-key check, and the job uses the AWS CLI that the `ubuntu-latest` runner image provides.

nodes.name: treetracker-wallet-admin-pr.yaml
nodes.summary: Pull request workflow "CI/CD Pipeline" that checks every PR on Node 20 with `npm ci --legacy-peer-deps`, `npm run lint` (ESLint on `./src`), `npm run build` and `npm test`. It copies the `client` job of build-release.yaml; its `npm run build:dev` and `client-bundle` upload steps require `github.event_name == 'push'`, so they never run on `pull_request` events.
nodes.languageNotes: The header comment mentions several Node versions, but the job has no matrix and uses only `node-version: '20'`. The `skip-ci` condition reads `github.event.head_commit.message`, which `pull_request` payloads do not carry, so the condition never skips the job.

nodes.name: .env
nodes.summary: Base environment file that Create React App loads for every script. It sets `REACT_APP_VERSION` to `$npm_package_version`, which dotenv-expand fills from the version npm reads out of `package.json`, but no file in `src/` or `public/` reads this variable today.

nodes.name: .env.development
nodes.summary: Development settings that point `REACT_APP_WALLET_API_ROOT` at the dev-k8s wallet API v2 root and set `USER_LOCALE` to `en-US`. Create React App loads this file for `npm start`, and the `build:dev` script loads it explicitly through `env-cmd`.
nodes.languageNotes: Create React App inlines only variables with the `REACT_APP_` prefix into the browser bundle, so `USER_LOCALE` does not reach `formatWithCommas` in `src/utils/formatting.js` at runtime and `Intl.NumberFormat` falls back to the browser default locale.

nodes.name: .env.production
nodes.summary: Sets `REACT_APP_WALLET_API_ROOT` to the prod-k8s wallet API v2 root. Create React App loads this file automatically for `react-scripts build`, so the plain `npm run build` script, which the deploy workflow runs for its `prod` choice, bakes the production API URL into the bundle.
nodes.languageNotes: `build:dev` and `build:test` also call `react-scripts build`, but `env-cmd` sets the variable first and dotenv never overrides a value that already exists, so their own `.env.*` file wins over this one.

nodes.name: .env.test
nodes.summary: Sets `REACT_APP_WALLET_API_ROOT` to the test-k8s wallet API v2 root. The `build:test` script loads it through `env-cmd` to produce test-environment bundles, and Create React App also loads it when `react-scripts test` runs Jest with NODE_ENV=test.

nodes.name: .releaserc.json
nodes.summary: semantic-release configuration that releases from numeric maintenance branches, `main`, and the `v1` and `v2` prerelease branches on the `beta` channel; its plugins analyze commits, write release notes into `CHANGELOG.md`, bump `package.json`, commit both with a `[skip ci]` message, and publish a GitHub release. The build-release and deploy workflows also `require()` this file to map a branch or version tag to its release channel and CDN target.
nodes.languageNotes: With `prerelease: true`, semantic-release uses the branch name as the prerelease identifier, which is why versions on the `v2` branch look like `2.1.0-v2.30`.

nodes.name: CHANGELOG.md
nodes.summary: Release history generated by semantic-release, from 1.0.0 (2023-10-10) to 2.1.0-v2.30 (2026-11-05), with Bug Fixes and Features lists that link each change to its commit. It traces the client from the first login, send-tokens, and transfers-table work, through wallet listing and managed wallet creation, to the v2 trust relationship pages, wallet customization (logo, hero), and the trusted, untrusted, and managed wallet tabs for sending tokens.
nodes.languageNotes: Some entries appear twice because changes first shipped on a prerelease line are listed again when a later version line releases them, and the sections are not strictly chronological (1.0.0-v1.22 from 2023-08-25 sits below 1.0.0-v1.23).

nodes.name: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
nodes.summary: Contributor Covenant 1.4 code of conduct that lists welcome and unacceptable behaviors, the duty of maintainers to act on violations, where the rules apply, and how to report abuse to the Greenstand project team by e-mail.

nodes.name: CONTRIBUTING.md
nodes.summary: Contributor guide that explains how to find and get assigned an issue by label, the branch and pull-request flow (it still names `v1` as the target branch, while recent releases ship from `v2`), how to rebase a fork on upstream, and a JavaScript style guide. Its style rules (2-space indent, semicolons, 80-character lines, single quotes, trailing commas) match the repo's `.prettierrc`.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project front page that describes the wallet admin panel (wallet owners view and transfer tokens, create sub wallets, and configure wallet appearance), lists use cases for Greenstand Impact Tokens, links the Figma design and user stories, and gives local setup steps that end with `npm install`, `npm start`, and http://localhost:3000. Its Node.js 18 setup steps conflict with the `engines` range (>= 19 < 21) in `package.json` and the Node 20 pinned in `.nvmrc`.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: npm manifest for the Create React App client at version 2.1.0-v2.30, built on React 18, MUI 5 with Emotion, React Router 6, axios, dayjs, jwt-decode, react-quill, and react-secure-storage. Its scripts wrap `react-scripts`, add `build:dev`, `build:test`, and `build:staging` variants that load `.env.development`, `.env.test`, and `.env.staging` through `env-cmd`, run ESLint over `src`, pin Node to >= 19 < 21, and let Jest transform axios.
nodes.languageNotes: `build:staging` points at `.env.staging`, which the repository does not contain, and `build:dev` renames the output folder to `build-dev`, the folder the build-release workflow uploads. `npm run lint` ignores the `eslintConfig` block because ESLint prefers the root `.eslintrc.json` in the same directory.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Create React App HTML shell for the wallet admin panel, titled "Treetracker Admin by Greenstand". It links manifest.json, favicon.ico and logo_192x192.png through %PUBLIC_URL%, loads the Google Analytics gtag.js tag inline, and holds the empty div#root that src/index.js mounts the React App into.
nodes.languageNotes: %PUBLIC_URL% is a Create React App build-time placeholder: react-scripts replaces it with the public path and injects the bundled script tags, so the file itself has no app script reference.

nodes.name: manifest.json
nodes.summary: Web app manifest that names the client "Greenstand Tree Tracker Wallet Admin Client" (short name "Tree Tracker Wallet Admin") and lists the favicon, 192px, 512px and maskable PNG icons for home-screen install. It starts at ./index.html in standalone display mode with a #76BB23 green theme color on a white background.
nodes.languageNotes: The icon with purpose "maskable" lets Android crop it to an adaptive shape. The theme_color here (#76BB23) differs from the theme-color meta tag in index.html (#000000).

nodes.name: robots.txt
nodes.summary: Crawler policy from the Create React App template: one rule for every user agent with an empty Disallow line, so search engines may crawl all paths of the deployed admin client.

nodes.name: .eslintignore
nodes.summary: Lists the paths ESLint skips: node_modules/, build/, coverage/, any __tests__/ folder, every *.test.* file, and src/stories. Because of the test patterns, the `npm run lint` step (`eslint ./src`) checks only production source, and neither src/stories nor a __tests__ folder exists in the repo today.

nodes.name: .npmrc
nodes.summary: Sets `engine-strict=true`, so npm refuses to install dependencies when the running Node version is outside the `engines.node` range `>= 19 < 21` in package.json. This turns the Node 19/20 requirement into a hard install gate instead of a warning.

nodes.name: .nvmrc
nodes.summary: Pins Node `20` for nvm users, a version inside the package.json `engines.node` range and the same `node-version: '20'` that the GitHub Actions workflows set. The commit that upgraded Node for semantic-release last changed it.

nodes.name: .prettierignore
nodes.summary: Tells Prettier to skip `.eslintrc.js`. The repo tracks its ESLint config as `.eslintrc.json`, so this single entry matches no current file.

nodes.name: quill.snow.css
nodes.summary: Local copy of the Quill Editor v1.3.7 Snow theme stylesheet that CustomizeWallet.js imports to style its ReactQuill rich-text editor, instead of loading the theme from the react-quill package. It styles the editor container, nine indent levels of numbered lists, the color, background, font and size format classes, the toolbar buttons and pickers, and the link, formula and video tooltip.
nodes.languageNotes: Numbers nested ordered lists with CSS counters: each `.ql-indent-N` item increments counter `list-N` and resets the deeper counters, and the `::before` content cycles decimal, lower-alpha and lower-roman by level.

nodes.name: index.css
nodes.summary: Global stylesheet that src/index.js loads at startup: a universal reset that removes default margin and padding and sets `box-sizing: border-box` on every element, plus a system UI font stack with font smoothing on `body`.

nodes.name: setupTests.js
nodes.summary: Jest setup file that `react-scripts test` runs before every test file. It registers the @testing-library/jest-dom matchers and globally mocks react-secure-storage, so `getItem('api-key')` returns a fixed mock string and the API modules that build the `TREETRACKER-API-KEY` header can run in tests.
nodes.languageNotes: The `jest.mock` factory sets `__esModule: true`, so its `default` object becomes the default export that `import secureLocalStorage from 'react-secure-storage'` receives. Many test files also call `jest.mock('react-secure-storage', ...)` with their own factory.

layers.name: Application Shell
layers.description: Boot and composition code that turns the Create React App HTML page into the running admin panel: the public index.html with its PWA manifest and robots file, the React 18 root in index.js with global CSS and web vitals, the App provider stack, and the ClientRoutes table that maps each URL to a page behind the login guard.

layers.name: Feature Pages
layers.description: Route-level screens for each wallet owner task (Login, Wallet home, Send Tokens, My Transfers, My Wallets, Trust Relationship, Customize Wallet, 404), with the feature-only tables, filters, side panels, dialogs, form helpers, validators and Emotion or MUI styled files that live next to them.

layers.name: Shared UI and Layout
layers.description: Reusable presentation pieces under src/components that many pages share: the MUI theme with Greenstand colors and Lato type, the signed-in layout with the top bar and collapsible side menu, the page header, the generic paginated Table, the Loader, Message and TabPanel widgets, the brand logo, and the vendored Quill Snow stylesheet.

layers.name: State Management
layers.description: React context stores in src/store that hold the session and the list state for the feature screens: the auth context and AuthProvider that keep the token and wallet profile, and the transfers, trust relationships and wallets contexts that own pagination, sorting, filters and data loading.

layers.name: API Client and Query Models
layers.description: The data access boundary to the wallet API: the shared axios apiClient with its base URL and auth headers, the wallets, transfers and trust relationship endpoint modules, the TransferFilter and TrustRelationShipFilter classes that build list query options, and the formatting helpers that turn filters into query strings and format numbers and dates.

layers.name: Tests
layers.description: Jest and React Testing Library suites that sit next to the code they cover (unit tests for validators and filter models, render tests for shared widgets and layout, page-level tests with mocked API calls), plus setupTests.js which registers jest-dom and the shared mocks before every test file.

layers.name: Project Configuration
layers.description: Files that set up the build and the runtime environment: the npm manifest with React, MUI and react-scripts and its scripts, the base, development, test and production .env files that pick the wallet API root, the Node version pins in .nvmrc and .npmrc, and the ESLint and Prettier ignore lists.

layers.name: CI/CD and Release
layers.description: GitHub Actions workflows that lint, test and build every pull request and branch push, cut versions with semantic-release, and deploy a chosen release tag to AWS S3 and CloudFront, together with the .releaserc.json file that defines the release branches and plugins.

layers.name: Documentation
layers.description: Project-level written guidance for people who work on the admin client: the README overview and setup guide, the contributor workflow and code style guide, the Contributor Covenant code of conduct, and the CHANGELOG that semantic-release generates.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to learn what the admin client is for. Wallet owners use it to see their Greenstand Impact Tokens, send tokens to other wallets, create sub wallets, and set how their wallet looks. The README also gives the local setup steps (`npm install`, `npm start`, then http://localhost:3000). Its Node.js 18 instructions are out of date, and Step 2 shows the Node version that the project really requires.

tour.title: Toolchain and Node Pins
tour.description: package.json shows a Create React App project: every script wraps `react-scripts`, and the main libraries are React 18, MUI 5 with Emotion, React Router 6, axios, and dayjs. Its `engines` field accepts Node `>= 19 < 21`, and .npmrc sets `engine-strict=true`, so `npm install` stops on any other Node version, including the Node 18 that the README names. .nvmrc pins Node `20`, the same version that the GitHub Actions workflows use. Note the `build:dev` and `build:test` scripts here, because Step 7 explains how they pick an API root.
tour.languageLesson: By default, the npm `engines` field only gives a warning. With `engine-strict=true` in .npmrc, npm turns a Node version mismatch into an install error. This keeps every contributor and every CI run on the same Node major version.

tour.title: Boot Sequence
tour.description: The browser loads public/index.html, the Create React App shell with an empty `div#root`, and src/index.js creates a React 18 root on that element and renders App. App.js stacks the app-wide providers from the outside in: the MUI ThemeProvider, a Day.js LocalizationProvider for the date pickers, BrowserRouter, and AuthProvider, around ClientRoutes. The `Layout` element that App.js passes as a child of ClientRoutes never renders, because ClientRoutes ignores its children. Step 5 shows that each route renders its own Layout.
tour.languageLesson: React context providers form a stack: a component can read a context only when an ancestor provides it, so the provider order in App.js matters. For example, AuthProvider calls the `useNavigate` hook, which needs a router above it, so AuthProvider must sit inside BrowserRouter.

tour.title: Session and Auth Context
tour.description: auth-context.js is the most depended-on file in the project. It creates AuthContext and documents the session shape: `isLoggedIn`, `token`, `wallet`, `login`, and `logout`. AuthProvider fills that shape with React state: on login it decodes the JWT with jwt-decode to build the wallet profile, always saves the wallet to localStorage, and saves the token only when the user checks remember-me. On logout it clears the token, the wallet, and the stored API key, then sends the user to /login.

tour.title: Routes Behind a Login Guard
tour.description: ClientRoutes maps each URL to a page and reads `isLoggedIn` from the AuthContext of Step 4. A small `ProtectedRoute` component sends a signed-out user to /login and renders an `<Outlet />` for a signed-in user. Every protected page (/, /my-transfers, /send-tokens, /list-wallets, /trust-relationship, /customize-wallet, and the `*` NotFound page) is wrapped in TrustRelationshipsProvider, TransfersProvider, and Layout, and /list-wallets also gets WalletsProvider. Only /login is outside the guard.
tour.languageLesson: React Router 6 layout routes: a parent `<Route element={<ProtectedRoute />}>` without a path wraps its child routes, and its `<Outlet />` renders the matched child. This puts one access check in front of many pages, so no page has to repeat it.

tour.title: Wallet API Client Layer
tour.description: All server calls go to the wallet API through a shared axios instance in apiClient.js. Its `baseURL` comes from `REACT_APP_WALLET_API_ROOT`, it sends a `TREETRACKER-API-KEY` header read from react-secure-storage, and chainable helpers such as `setAuthHeader(token)` add the bearer token from Step 4. The endpoint modules wrap it per resource: wallets.js lists, creates, and updates wallets, while transfers.js and trust_relationships.js list items with query strings that `makeQueryString` in formatting.js builds. Some action calls, such as accepting a transfer or deleting a trust relationship, skip apiClient and call native `fetch` with the same headers built by hand.
tour.languageLesson: React hooks work only while a component renders. The 401 interceptor in apiClient.js calls `useNavigate()` from a plain module, which React does not allow, so a 401 response ends in an error instead of a redirect to /login. Code outside components must redirect another way, for example with `window.location` or a router object that is passed in.

tour.title: API Root per Environment
tour.description: The `REACT_APP_WALLET_API_ROOT` variable that Step 6 reads comes from these files: .env.development, .env.test, and .env.production each point it at a different wallet API v2 root. Create React App loads .env.development for `npm start`, .env.production for `npm run build`, and .env.test for `react-scripts test`, while the `build:dev` and `build:test` scripts load .env.development and .env.test explicitly through `env-cmd`. The base .env file sets `REACT_APP_VERSION`, which no code reads yet. The `build:staging` script names a .env.staging file that the repository does not contain.
tour.languageLesson: Create React App writes environment variables into the bundle at build time, so a change needs a new build. It exposes only names that start with `REACT_APP_` (plus a few such as `NODE_ENV`). Thus `USER_LOCALE` in .env.development never reaches the browser, and `formatWithCommas` in formatting.js falls back to the browser's default locale.

tour.title: Login Flow
tour.description: The login page joins the pieces from Steps 4 to 7. The user enters a wallet name, a password, and an API key, and the pure helpers in loginValidator.js return an error text for an empty or too-long value. On submit, Login.js saves the API key in react-secure-storage, sets it on apiClient, and posts the wallet and password to `${REACT_APP_WALLET_API_ROOT}/auth`. A 200 response gives a token that goes to `authContext.login(token, isRemember)`, and a failure removes the stored API key and shows an error message.

tour.title: Feature Stores and Filter Models
tour.description: The list screens keep their data in React context stores, not in the pages. Each store holds pagination, sorting, filter, rows, total count, and loading state, and reloads through the API modules of Step 6 when one of them changes; TransfersContext and TrustRelationshipsContext also count the pending items that need the user to act. The filter values are TransferFilter and TrustRelationShipFilter objects, which turn the chosen options into the lowercase query parameters that the API expects. Each store exports a hook, such as `useTransfersContext`, that throws an error when a component uses it outside its provider.
tour.languageLesson: The provider-plus-hook pattern: a module creates a context, exports a Provider that owns the state and the side effects (a `useEffect` with a dependency list such as `[pagination, filter, sorting, refetch]`), and exports a hook that wraps `useContext`. The guard in the hook turns a missing provider into a clear error instead of an undefined value.

tour.title: Theme, Layout, and Shared Widgets
tour.description: theme.js, the second most depended-on file, defines the MUI theme for the whole panel: Lato type, the Greenstand green palette, and style overrides for buttons, tables, and alerts. Layout.js pairs the collapsible side Menu (with the TopMenu bar and its logout icon) with the content area, and it reads the pending counts from TrustRelationshipsContext and TransfersContext to show menu badges. Because Layout calls both store hooks, ClientRoutes in Step 5 must wrap every page in both providers. The generic Table (paginated and sortable, used by My Wallets) and the Message alert banner are shared widgets that the pages in the next steps reuse.

tour.title: Wallet Home and Management
tour.description: The home page (/) loads the signed-in wallet and its pending transfers, then shows the wallet header, the about text, and the token balance. My Wallets (/list-wallets) lists wallets in the shared Table with a scope selector for all, child, or managed wallets, and gets its pagination and sorting from WalletsContext. CreateManagedWallet opens a dialog that checks the name, calls `createWallet` with the session token, and asks the page to reload its list. Customize Wallet lets the owner edit the display name, the rich-text about text (react-quill), the logo, and the hero image, and each field saves on its own through `updateWallet`.

tour.title: Sending Tokens
tour.description: Send Tokens is the core task of the panel and the page with the most dependencies. SendTokens.js holds the selected sender wallet, its balance, and its pending outgoing amount, and shows three tabs: Managed Wallets, Trusted Wallets, and All Wallets. SendTokensForm serves the first two tabs with sender and receiver pickers, while SendToUntrustedWallets serves All Wallets with a free-text receiver field; both check the amount against the available tokens and ask for confirmation in a dialog. The helpers in sendTokenHandlers.js post to /transfers, update the sender balance, and turn API errors into messages through a callbacks object of state setters.
tour.languageLesson: When a component passes its state setters to a helper in a callbacks object, the async transfer logic can live in plain functions outside the component. The component then only renders, and you can read or test the helper without rendering anything.

tour.title: Transfers and Trust Requests
tour.description: My Transfers and Trust Relationship use the same design: a paginated, sortable table fed by its store from Step 9, highlighted rows for items that wait for the user, and a side panel that opens on a row click. TableFilters writes a new TransferFilter into TransfersContext when the user picks a status or a date range. TransferSidePanel offers Accept and Decline to the receiving wallet, or Cancel to the sending wallet, for a pending transfer. The trust relationship side panel offers Accept and Decline when a request targets the user's wallet or a managed wallet, else Delete, and then sets `refetch` so that the store reloads the table.

tour.title: Tests and Test Setup
tour.description: Jest and React Testing Library tests sit next to the code that they cover, and `react-scripts test` runs setupTests.js before every test file. That file registers the jest-dom matchers and mocks react-secure-storage, so the API modules from Step 6 can build their `TREETRACKER-API-KEY` header in tests. ClientRoutes.test.js renders the routes as a signed-in user and checks the layout and the menu, while the page tests mock `getTransfers` or `getTrustRelationships`, render the page inside its providers, and check the table, the pagination, and the filters. package.json also tells Jest to transform axios, because axios 1.x ships as an ES module.
tour.languageLesson: `jest.mock('module', factory)` in a setup file replaces a module for every test. Here it swaps react-secure-storage, which needs browser storage, for an object of `jest.fn()` stubs that returns a fixed `api-key` value.

tour.title: CI, Release, and Deploy
tour.description: Every pull request runs the "CI/CD Pipeline" workflow on Node 20, which lints, builds, and tests the client. Every branch push starts "Build and Release", but its prepare job reads .releaserc.json and continues only for `main` and for `v1` and `v2` (the `beta` channel); it then runs the same checks and semantic-release, which writes CHANGELOG.md and bumps the version in package.json. That workflow then syncs the `npm run build:dev` bundle to the S3 bucket and CloudFront distribution that the `DEV_CDN_*` secrets (channel `main`) or the `DEV_STAGING_CDN_*` secrets (channel `beta`) name. The manual "Deploy" workflow takes a release tag (input `version`) and an input `env` of `dev`, `test`, or `prod`, and builds with `npm run build:dev`, `npm run build:test`, or `npm run build`, so each choice picks one of the .env files from Step 7.
tour.languageLesson: In GitHub Actions, `on: pull_request` and `on: push` choose the trigger, `needs` orders the jobs, and an `if` condition can skip a job. Here a prepare job writes the channel and the secret names to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, and later jobs read them as `needs.prepare.outputs.*` and look up the real secret with `secrets[...]`.
